title: Ink, Wax, and What They Can't Do

sets.relationshipLabel: object and the substance it is made of
sets.explanation: A candle is made of wax and an envelope is made of paper — each object names the raw substance that constitutes it.
A seal guards against tampering just as a blotter guards against a smudge — each is a safeguard against a specific kind of spoiling.

sets.relationshipLabel: earlier and later state of one span
sets.explanation: A draft becomes a final and a taper becomes a stub — each pair marks the start and end of the same process, one in writing and one in burning.

sets.relationshipLabel: thing and the one property it can never have
sets.explanation: A flame can never have weight and smoke can never hold a shape — each names a property permanently and necessarily denied to it.
